items.description:
The Barber's Range is a barbershop operating as part of a small chain with several branches across Cape Town, with this location trading from 3Arts Village in Plumstead. The shop focuses on precision haircuts and classic barbering, offering shaves, beard trims, head shaves and modern cuts, with hot towels and waxing also available.

Trimming and shaving are treated as a craft rather than a quick service, with real attention given to prepping and softening the skin before a blade is used. The barbershop suits anyone after a traditional, unhurried cut rather than a rushed walk-in trim. Trading from Shop GF-S31 on Main Road in Plumstead, it opens Monday to Thursday from 8am to 7pm, Friday 8am to 1pm and 2pm to 7pm, Saturday 8am to 5pm, and Sunday 8am to 3pm.

The Coffee Co Cafe is a neighbourhood coffee shop in Milnerton built around a casual, all-day menu rather than a strict breakfast-and-lunch split. Coffee is made to order rather than pre-batched, and the space suits people who want to linger, work or meet over a cup rather than grab and go, with free WiFi available throughout.

The menu runs alongside the coffee programme with light meals and snacks suited to a relaxed daytime visit, the kind of spot locals use for a work catch-up, a quick breakfast or an afternoon break rather than a formal sit-down meal. Set on Heron Crescent in Milnerton, on the Atlantic seaboard side of Cape Town, the cafe draws a mix of residents, remote workers and passers-by looking for a dependable, unhurried coffee stop.

The Courier Guy is one of South Africa's established domestic and international courier networks, moving parcels and documents through overnight, economy and same-day delivery options between homes, businesses and its branch network. This outlet operates as a service kiosk rather than a full branch, giving the surrounding community a local counter to drop off, collect and pay for parcels without travelling into town.

Customers can book a collection, hand over an already-booked waybill, or collect a parcel sent to the kiosk for them, which suits a busy retail environment where people are already running other errands. Trading from inside Khaya Corner on the corner of Govan Mbeki and Oscar Mpetha Roads in Mandela Park, Khayelitsha, the kiosk is open Monday to Friday from 8am to 5pm and Saturdays until 1pm, closed on Sundays.

The Crazy Store is a well-known South African variety retailer with branches in malls and centres across the country, known for stretching a household budget across stationery, toys, homeware, party supplies, gifts and seasonal lines under one roof. The format is built around low prices and a constantly changing mix of stock rather than a narrow specialist range.

This branch trades from Erica Square in Belhar, giving the surrounding suburb a nearby stop for everyday odds and ends, school supplies and small gifts without a trip to a larger mall. It keeps hours that suit shoppers doing a full round of weekend errands, opening Monday to Friday from 9am to 6pm, Saturdays from 9am to 3pm and Sundays from 9am to 2pm.

The Crazy Store is a South African variety retailer selling homeware, stationery, toys and gifts at affordable prices, and this branch trades from inside Capricorn Square in Muizenberg. The centre's own store directory places it among a cluster of everyday retailers, including Ackermans, Mr Price, Pep and Jam Clothing for clothing, Clicks for health and beauty, and Capitec Bank and Standard Bank for banking.

That mix of neighbours makes the store a practical stop for households doing a weekly shopping round in the area rather than a standalone destination. Open Monday to Friday from 9am to 6pm, Saturdays from 8am to 5pm and Sundays from 9am to 1pm, it fits around the wider centre's own trading pattern on Prince George Drive in Muizenberg.

The Crazy Store is a national value and variety chain found in shopping centres across South Africa, stocking household goods, toys, stationery, gifts and seasonal items at budget prices. The appeal is less a single specialty than a broad, frequently refreshed range that lets a shopper tick off several small purchases in one visit.

This branch trades from Strand Square on Fagan Street in Strand, serving the surrounding residential area with a low-cost alternative to a dedicated toy shop, stationer or homeware store. Its hours are built around a shorter Friday and a full Saturday trading day, running Monday to Thursday from 8.30am to 5.30pm, Friday 8am to 2pm, Saturday 8am to 4pm, and Sundays and public holidays from 9am to 2pm.

The Fat German is a delicatessen and butchery trading as a specialist meat and deli counter rather than a general grocer, listed in local business directories under its Facebook page name of deli and butchery. The focus is on quality cuts and prepared deli items such as sausages and cold meats, serving customers who want a proper butcher's counter rather than a supermarket meat aisle.

Shoppers can expect the kind of individual attention a small, specialist shop offers, from advice on a cut of meat to picking up ready-made deli items for lunch or a braai. Trading from Shop 5 in Meadowridge Shopping Centre on Howard Drive, Meadowridge, the shop opens Monday to Friday from 8am to 5pm and Saturdays until 1pm, and is closed on Sundays.

The Health Team is a medical centre bringing together several kinds of care under one roof rather than operating as a single-doctor practice, with general practitioners working alongside a psychiatrist and a physiotherapist on site. That combination lets patients deal with everyday health concerns, mental health support and physical rehabilitation without being referred across town for each one.

The practice is listed with the national healthcare directory Medpages, which records it as a private clinic in Mouille Point, and with the booking platform Recomed, which lists its practitioners for appointments. Based at 129 Beach Road in Mouille Point, close to the Atlantic seaboard promenade, the centre keeps weekday office hours from 8.30am to 5pm and is closed over weekends.

The Kind Kitchen is a small vegan restaurant built around seasonal, plant-based comfort food rather than a fixed, year-round menu, using locally grown and sourced produce so dishes shift with what is available. It is listed on Eat Out's venue directory alongside Cape Town's wider restaurant scene, and its own site sets out that seasonal, produce-led approach as the kitchen's main idea.

Based at Woodstock Brewery on Albert Road, the restaurant suits diners after vegan cooking that still reads as comfort food rather than a strict health-food menu, and its small size keeps the kitchen close to its ingredients. It trades Monday from 10am to 3pm, Tuesday to Friday from 10am to 8pm and Saturday from 10am to 3pm, closed on Sundays.

The Lounge On Kromboom is a restaurant serving a Cape Malay-inspired menu of curries, grills and burgers alongside other casual dining dishes, reviewed on both Eat Out's venue directory and Tripadvisor as a sit-down spot rather than a takeaway counter. The menu leans on the spiced, slow-cooked flavours associated with Cape Malay cooking rather than a generic grill-house card.

Operating from the first floor of Kromboom Convenience Centre, the restaurant suits groups and families looking for a relaxed meal with some local flavour rather than a formal booking. It is closed on Mondays, then trades Tuesday to Thursday from 11am to 9pm, Friday from 2pm to 10pm, Saturday from 11am to 10pm and Sunday from 11am to 9pm, on Kromboom Road in Crawford.

Tirepoint is a tyre fitment and repair centre offering wheel alignment, wheel balancing and puncture repairs alongside general tyre replacement, backed by a national breakdown call centre that operates around the clock. The company's own site lists branches beyond the Western Cape, including Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal and the Free State, so this outlet forms part of a wider network rather than standing alone.

That network means a customer stranded with a tyre problem outside normal hours can still reach a call centre for assistance, even though the workshop itself keeps standard weekday hours. Based on Milan Road in Matroosfontein, the centre trades Monday to Friday from 8am to 4.45pm, serving motorists and fleet operators across the surrounding northern suburbs who need fitment, repairs or alignment work done properly.

TOPS at SPAR Stellenberg is a liquor store operating under the TOPS franchise banner attached to the Stellenberg Spar Centre, stocking wine, spirits, beer and ready-to-drink beverages rather than running as an independent bottle store. The TOPS format pairs a dedicated liquor counter with the convenience of an attached supermarket, letting shoppers pick up drinks on the same trip as their groceries.

Listed in local business directories as a liquor store on Haarlem Street, the branch serves the Stellenberg and wider Bellville community with a stock range built for everyday drinking and entertaining rather than a specialist wine cellar. It keeps long trading hours to match, open Monday to Saturday from 9am to 8pm and Sundays from 11am to 6pm.

Tribe Coffee is a specialty coffee roastery and café that roasts its own beans on site rather than buying in from another supplier, a point reflected in its listings on both Eat Out and Tripadvisor. The café side serves that roasted coffee alongside a simple food offering suited to a coffee-first visit rather than a full restaurant menu.

Based at the Woodstock Foundry on Albert Road, the café draws in coffee enthusiasts, local office workers and visitors exploring Woodstock's creative precinct rather than passing foot traffic alone. It trades Monday to Friday from 7am to 4pm and Saturdays from 9am to 2pm, closing on Sundays, hours that suit a weekday coffee routine more than a leisurely weekend brunch crowd.

Ukhanyo Primary School is a no-fee public primary school listed on the Western Cape Education Department's own facility register, offering Grade R to Grade 7 schooling to children in Masiphumelele. As a no-fee school, it falls into the public system's funding category for communities where school fees would otherwise be a barrier to enrolment.

The school serves the township's families directly, giving local children a primary education within walking distance rather than a daily commute to another suburb, and is also listed in general business directories alongside other public primary schools in the area. Based on Pokela Road in Masiphumelele, its premises are accessible from 8am to 5pm on weekdays and closed over weekends.

Usave is Shoprite Holdings' discount supermarket format, built around a smaller store footprint and a trimmed range of everyday groceries sold at low prices rather than the fuller aisles of a standard Shoprite or Checkers. The format targets budget-conscious households doing a regular grocery shop rather than a once-off big basket trip.

This branch serves the Colorado Park area of Mitchells Plain, giving residents a nearby, affordable grocery option without needing to travel to a larger supermarket. It keeps weekend trading alongside weekday hours to suit a working household's shopping pattern, open Monday to Friday from 9am to 7pm, Saturdays from 8am to 6pm and Sundays from 8am to 2pm, at the corner of Highlands Drive and Weltevreden Parkway.

Usave is the discount supermarket banner run by Shoprite Holdings, stripping back the range and store size of a full Shoprite to focus on everyday grocery staples at low prices. It is aimed at shoppers watching a tight household budget rather than those after a wide selection of specialty or imported goods.

This outlet trades on Ottery Road in Ottery, giving the surrounding community a straightforward, no-frills grocery stop within the suburb rather than a drive to a bigger centre. Its hours cover most of the week, running Monday to Friday from 8am to 6pm, Saturdays from 8am to 5pm and Sundays from 8am to 2pm, making it a practical option for a quick top-up shop as well as a full weekly grocery run.

Utah Spur is a branch of Spur Steak Ranches, the long-running South African family steakhouse chain built around grills, burgers, ribs and a self-service salad bar alongside a menu for younger diners. The chain's familiar format pairs casual, sit-down dining with activities for children at many branches, making it a regular choice for family outings rather than a quick bite.

Trading from Bothasig Square, the restaurant draws families and groups from the surrounding Bothasig and Milnerton area who want a reliable, mid-range meal without booking a formal restaurant. It keeps long hours across the week, open Monday to Thursday from 8.30am to 9pm, Friday and Saturday from 8.30am to 10pm and Sunday from 8.30am to 9pm.

Van Schaik is a long-standing South African bookstore chain with roots in academic bookselling, stocking textbooks and study guides alongside general fiction, non-fiction, stationery and gifts at its retail branches. The chain's academic background sets it apart from a purely general bookshop, giving it a stronger textbook and reference range than most competitors.

This branch trades from Parow Centre on Voortrekker Road, serving students, schools and general readers in Parow and the surrounding northern suburbs with both curriculum materials and everyday reading. It keeps hours suited to a shopping centre, open Monday to Friday from 9am to 5.30pm, Saturdays from 9.30am to 4pm and Sundays from 9am to 1pm.

Vitacare Pharmacy is part of the Vitacare Group's network of community pharmacies, offering prescription dispensing alongside everyday health, wellness and personal-care retail rather than operating as a large chain pharmacy. The group model lets individual branches keep a community feel while sharing buying power and systems across the network.

This branch operates from inside the Kromboom Medi-Centre in Crawford, placing it alongside other healthcare practitioners rather than in a standalone retail unit, which suits patients collecting medication after seeing a doctor on site. Its hours are split around a midday break on weekdays, running Monday to Thursday from 9am to 1pm and 2pm to 6pm, Friday 9am to 12.30pm and 2.30pm to 6pm, and Saturdays from 9am to 1pm, closed on Sundays.

Vitacare Pharmacy is a branch of the Vitacare Group, a South African network of community pharmacies that combines prescription dispensing with retail health, beauty and wellness products under a shared group identity rather than a single big-chain banner. Being part of a group gives the branch access to broader stock and systems while still functioning as a local pharmacy counter.

This outlet trades from inside Riverside Mall in Rondebosch, putting it within reach of mall shoppers and the surrounding university and residential area. It opens Monday to Thursday from 8am to 6pm, Friday from 8am to 12.45pm and 2pm to 6pm, Saturdays from 8am to 2pm and Sundays from 9am to 1pm.

Vizi Hair is a hair salon offering a full colour and styling menu, including balayage, highlights, permanent straightening, keratin treatments, extensions and weaves alongside standard cuts, as listed on its own booking page with the salon platform Fresha. That range of colour and chemical services puts it closer to a specialist colour studio than a basic cut-and-blow-dry salon.

The breadth of services suits clients after a significant change, such as a full colour correction or an extension fitting, as much as those booking a regular trim. Based on Oxford Street in Durbanville, the salon is closed on Mondays, then trades Tuesday to Friday from 8am to 5pm and Saturdays from 8am to 1.30pm, closed again on Sundays.

VO2 Gear is a sportswear and sporting goods retailer stocking performance clothing and equipment for athletes, the kind of specialist shop that sits apart from a general clothing store by focusing on kit built for training and competition rather than everyday fashion. Retailers in this category typically supply both individual athletes and sports clubs needing matching kit for a team.

Trading from the first floor of Westlake Shopping Centre, the store serves runners, cyclists and other sportspeople across the Westlake and wider Constantia valley area looking for gear suited to their specific sport rather than a generic sportswear rack. It is open Monday to Saturday from 9am to 5pm and Sundays from 9am to 3pm, from Shop 27 on Westlake Drive.

Walmer Butchery is a full-range butchery known for a wide selection of sosaties and kebabs alongside its everyday fresh meat counter, a specialty that distinguishes it from a plain cuts-and-mince butcher. That focus on skewered, marinated meat suits customers planning a braai as much as those doing a regular meat shop.

The butchery is listed in local business directories as a meat retailer in Walmer Estate, serving the surrounding residential community with a neighbourhood counter rather than a supermarket meat aisle. Based on Coronation Road in Walmer Estate, it trades Monday to Friday from 8am to 5.30pm and Saturdays from 8am to 3pm.

Warren's Pharmacy is a community pharmacy offering prescription dispensing alongside everyday health, wellness and personal-care products, the kind of independent-style pharmacy that serves as a neighbourhood health counter rather than a large retail chain. Pharmacies of this kind typically combine a dispensary with advice on over-the-counter medication and general health queries.

Based on Main Road in Fish Hoek, the pharmacy serves the Fish Hoek community and surrounding False Bay suburbs, giving residents a local option for both prescriptions and everyday health needs. It keeps notably long hours for a pharmacy, open Monday to Saturday from 8.30am to 7pm and Sundays from 9am to 7pm, useful for evening and weekend medication needs as well as weekday visits.

Wellness Warehouse is a South African health and wellness retail chain stocking supplements, vitamins, natural remedies, health foods and natural body-care products rather than running as a standard pharmacy or supermarket health aisle. The chain is built around natural and complementary health choices, giving shoppers an alternative to mainstream pharmacy brands for that kind of product.

This branch trades from Glengarry Shopping Centre in Brackenfell North, serving the surrounding Brackenfell and Vredekloof community with a dedicated health-focused retail option rather than a general grocery stop. It is open Monday to Friday from 9am to 6pm, Saturdays from 9am to 5pm and Sundays from 9am to 1pm, from Shop 12 and 13 on De Bron Road.

Wimpy is one of South Africa's longest-running family restaurant chains, known for all-day breakfasts, burgers and classic diner-style meals served in a sit-down setting rather than a fast-food counter. Branches typically combine table service with a menu built for families, making the chain a familiar stop in malls and shopping centres across the country.

This branch trades from inside Longbeach Mall in Noordhoek, giving shoppers and the surrounding Noordhoek and Sun Valley community a dependable breakfast and lunch option attached to their centre visit. It opens Monday to Friday from 8am to 6pm, Saturdays from 8am to 5pm and Sundays from 8am to 3pm, from Shop G14b on the corner of Buller Louw Boulevard and Sunnydale Road.

Wimpy is a well-established South African family restaurant chain built around all-day breakfasts, burgers and diner-style meals, and this branch operates as a drive-thru format attached to a Sasol convenience centre rather than a mall-based sit-down restaurant. The drive-thru setup suits travellers and commuters along the West Coast road as much as local sit-down diners.

Running around the clock, the restaurant gives Melkbosstrand residents and passing travellers a meal option at any hour, from a late-night snack to an early breakfast before the coastal road. Based on Birkenhead Drive in Melkbosstrand, its round-the-clock trading makes it a dependable stop for shift workers and holidaymakers alike, unlike most of its mall-based sister branches that close in the evening.

Woolworths is one of South Africa's major supermarket groups, known for a strong food offering built around prepared meals, fresh produce and own-brand groceries alongside household goods, positioned above most budget supermarket rivals on price. Its food-focused branches, often called Woolworths Food, tend to be smaller format stores suited to a city or lifestyle precinct rather than a full hypermarket.

This branch trades from inside the LifeStyle Centre on Kloof Street in Gardens, serving the city bowl's residents, office workers and visitors with a convenient grocery stop in a pedestrian-friendly retail strip. It is open from 8am to 7pm Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 8am to 5pm on Wednesdays and Sundays, and 8am to 6pm on Saturdays.

Woolworths is a major South African supermarket group whose food stores concentrate on fresh produce, prepared meals and own-brand groceries rather than trying to match a hypermarket's full range of non-food lines. Its smaller-format stores, often branded Woolworths Food, suit neighbourhood and strip-mall locations better than a large standalone supermarket would, and work well for a quick top-up between bigger grocery trips elsewhere.

This branch operates from The Old Bakery shopping centre on Main Road in Lakeside, giving the surrounding Lakeside and Muizenberg area a nearby grocery stop for prepared meals, fresh produce and household basics. It keeps even hours across the week, open Monday to Friday from 8.30am to 7pm and Saturdays and Sundays from 8.30am to 6pm.

Woolworths Food is the grocery-focused format of South Africa's Woolworths group, built around fresh produce, prepared meals, a bakery and own-brand groceries rather than the broader clothing and homeware range carried by the group's larger department stores. Shoppers can expect the same prepared-meal counters and deli range found at other Woolworths Food branches, alongside everyday pantry essentials.

This branch trades from Strand Square on Fagan Street in Strand, giving the seaside town's residents a dependable grocery stop within their own shopping centre rather than a drive to a larger supermarket elsewhere. It serves the Strand community alongside the centre's other retailers, functioning as a convenient food stop for shoppers doing a full round of errands at Strand Square rather than a single quick purchase.

Workshop17 is a South African premium coworking brand offering hot-desking, private offices and meeting rooms for members rather than a budget shared-desk setup, with locations designed around a hospitality-style member experience including barista coffee and curated events. The brand has grown across several Cape Town, Johannesburg and Durban locations, each fitted out to its own building rather than an identical template.

This branch occupies 32 Kloof Street in Gardens, putting members close to the city bowl's restaurants, shops and the wider Kloof Street business strip rather than an office park. It suits freelancers, small teams and corporate satellite staff who want flexible, professional space without a long lease, open Monday to Thursday from 7.30am to 5.30pm and Fridays from 7.30am to 5pm, closed over weekends.

Zeekoevlei High School is a public secondary school providing Grade 8 to Grade 12 education within the standard public schooling system, serving the surrounding Lotus River community rather than operating as an independent or fee-heavy institution. As with most public high schools in the area, it follows the national curriculum and caters mainly to learners from the immediate neighbourhood.

The school gives local families a secondary education option within their own suburb, reducing the need for a long daily commute to a school elsewhere in the southern suburbs. Based on 7th Avenue in Lotus River, it operates during standard South African school terms and hours, forming part of the public education network serving Lotus River and the neighbouring communities of the Cape Flats.

1890 House Sushi & Grill is a sushi and grill restaurant operating from a converted semi-detached house rather than a purpose-built restaurant space, a setting reviewed on both Tripadvisor and Eat Out's venue listings for the area. The house format gives the restaurant a more domestic, lived-in feel than a typical standalone restaurant shopfront.

The restaurant has served Observatory's mix of students, academics and NGO workers for more than 18 years, building a loyal local following in a suburb known for its student and creative community rather than a tourist strip. Based on Trill Road in Observatory, it trades Monday to Saturday from 11.30am to 9.45pm and Sundays from 11.30am to 9.30pm.

A J North (Pty) Ltd is a South African manufacturer producing toiletries and toothbrushes rather than operating as a retailer, supplying affordable beauty, haircare and household products that are sold on through other stores rather than from its own shopfront. Listings for the company in business directories place it in the toiletries manufacturing category rather than general retail or wholesale.

The company has been manufacturing in the sector for over 100 years, a long operating history for a South African manufacturer in this category. Based at 38 Thor Circle in the Thornton industrial area of Cape Town, the business runs from a factory and office premises rather than a public-facing store, open Monday to Friday from 8am to 5pm and closed over weekends.

Ackermans is one of South Africa's largest value fashion retailers, selling affordable clothing, footwear and homeware for women, men, children and babies rather than competing on premium brands or high fashion. The chain's model is built around frequent, low-priced ranges that turn over quickly, making it a regular stop for budget-conscious family shopping rather than an occasional treat purchase.

This branch trades from Shop 33 in Delft Mall, giving the Delft community a nearby option for school uniforms, everyday clothing and baby essentials without a trip to a larger mall. It keeps retail hours that stretch into the evening on weekdays, open Monday to Friday from 9am to 8pm, Saturdays from 9am to 6pm and Sundays from 9am to 5pm, at the corner of Hindle and Delft Main Road.

All Road Tyres is a tyre dealer and reclaimer established in 2001, supplying reclaimed tyres mainly to the truck industry rather than running as a general passenger-vehicle tyre fitment centre. The business is listed with Michelin's own dealer locator and in regional business directories under tyre dealers, pointing to a trade-facing rather than retail-facing operation.

Reclaimed truck tyres offer fleet operators a lower-cost alternative to new tyres for vehicles that do not need top-tier performance, which is the gap this kind of business typically fills. Operating from a plant on Killarney Avenue in Killarney Gardens, the company has supplied the trucking sector in the area for over two decades, trading Monday to Friday from 8am to 4.45pm.

All Things Earthly is an organic and ethical grocery and lifestyle shop stocking locally grown produce, preservative-free groceries, natural body-care products and eco-friendly household goods, a focus covered in a local lifestyle feature on sustainable shopping in Cape Town. The shop is built around sustainable, conscious living rather than running as a general health shop or standard grocer.

Based inside Noordhoek Farm Village, the shop fits naturally alongside the village's other small, farm-style retailers, drawing shoppers who want to buy organic and package-light rather than from a conventional supermarket shelf. It trades every day of the week, open Monday to Sunday from 9am to 5pm, at 1 Village Lane in Noordhoek Farm Village.

Alpine Primary School is a no-fee public primary school governed as a Section 21 school, meaning its own governing body manages the school's budget rather than relying entirely on provincial administration, a status recorded in school directory listings for the Beacon Valley area. That Section 21 status is typically given to schools whose governing bodies have shown they can handle their own finances responsibly.

The school serves the Beacon Valley community within Mitchells Plain, giving local children primary schooling close to home under South Africa's no-fee school system. Based on the corner of Alpine and Glider Street in Beacon Valley, it operates during standard school hours, open Monday to Friday from 7am to 3pm and closed on weekends.

Alta Bay is a boutique guesthouse set on the slopes of Table Mountain in Higgovale, offering six individually designed rooms rather than a standard, identical room layout found at larger hotels. Reviews on both HotelPlanner and Tripadvisor describe the property's mountain and sea views as a particular draw, alongside its smaller, more personal scale.

Guests can expect on-site spa treatments and dining as part of the stay, giving the guesthouse a resort-style feel despite its intimate size, rather than having to leave the property for meals or treatments. Based on Invermark Crescent in Higgovale, just above the city bowl, the guesthouse suits travellers looking for a quieter, boutique stay with mountain views over a large hotel in the centre of town.

Anatoli has served Turkish and Mediterranean cuisine on Napier Street since 1984, making it one of the longer-standing restaurants in the De Waterkant area, a history noted in both local food blog coverage and its Eat Out venue listing. The restaurant operates as a dinner-only venue rather than offering lunch or breakfast service.

It is housed in a Victorian warehouse building dating to 1904, giving the restaurant a distinctive, atmospheric setting rather than a modern restaurant fit-out, which suits diners looking for a sense of occasion with their meal. Based at 24 Napier Street in De Waterkant, the restaurant trades Monday to Saturday from 6pm to 10.30pm and is closed on Sundays.

Atlantic Meat is a butchery offering a full range of quality meat cuts, operating as part of a small chain of butcheries with several branches across Cape Town rather than a single independent shop. The group's own website lists its branch network, pointing to a business that has grown its butchery format across more than one suburb.

That chain structure typically means more consistent stock and pricing across branches than a one-off independent butcher, while still functioning as a local meat counter at each location. Based on Voortrekker Road in Maitland, the butchery serves the surrounding Maitland and Voortrekker Road corridor community, trading Monday to Friday from 8am to 6pm, Saturdays from 8am to 4pm and Sundays from 8am to 2pm.

Auto Panel Repair Centre is a panelbeating and spraypainting workshop carrying out autobody and collision repairs on all vehicle makes rather than specialising in one brand, backed by a 3-year workmanship warranty according to its own website. That warranty period is longer than many independent panel shops offer, signalling a workshop confident in the durability of its repair work.

The business handles the kind of work that follows a collision or minor accident, from dent and panel repair through to a full respray, serving motorists across Ottery and the surrounding southern suburbs who need a vehicle restored to its pre-accident condition. Based on Shawcamp Road in Ottery, the workshop operates as a dedicated collision repair centre rather than a general mechanical garage.

AVBOB Khayelitsha is a funeral parlour and insurance branch of the AVBOB Mutual Assurance Society, one of South Africa's largest funeral service providers, offering both funeral policies and the practical arrangement of funeral services rather than just one or the other. The branch is listed with the National Funeral Directors Association, which records it as a registered funeral service provider for the area.

As a mutual society, AVBOB channels its funeral business back to members rather than outside shareholders, a structure that has kept it a dominant name in South African funeral cover for generations. Based in Ilitha Park, Khayelitsha, the branch serves the local community's funeral and bereavement needs, open Monday to Friday from 8am to 4.30pm, Saturdays from 8.30am to midday and closed on Sundays.

B74 is a bar and bistro with two bars and a relaxed courtyard braai area, a layout set out on its own website alongside its Durban Road address in Mowbray. The menu is known locally for its mussels, curly fries and chicken wings, dishes that keep the venue firmly in casual bar-food territory rather than fine dining.

The combination of an indoor bar, a second bar and an outdoor braai courtyard gives the venue several different settings for a night out, from a quick after-work drink to a longer group booking around the braai area. Based at 74 Durban Road in Mowbray, the bistro opens Monday to Friday from midday to 9pm and weekends from 10am to 9pm.

Be-Dazzle Hair and Beauty Salon is a hair, beauty and slimming salon offering hair colouring and treatments alongside manicures, pedicures, waxing and laser hair removal, a service list carried on both its Facebook page and its listing with a local spa directory. Combining hair, beauty and slimming services under one roof means clients can book several kinds of treatment in a single salon rather than visiting separate specialists.

The salon has operated from Access Park in Kenilworth since 2012, giving it over a decade of trading history in the same centre. It suits clients after a fuller beauty routine, from colour and treatments to waxing and laser sessions, rather than a quick cut alone. It opens Monday to Wednesday from 8am to 5pm, Thursday and Friday until 6pm, Saturdays until 5pm and Sundays from 9am to 2pm.

Belhar Primary School is a public primary school with around 1,100 learners, a scale confirmed on the school's own website alongside its contact details for the Acanthus Circle campus. The school runs under the motto 'Labour En-Nobles', reflecting an emphasis on effort and achievement across its academic, sporting and cultural programmes.

With over a thousand learners, the school is a sizeable part of the Belhar community's primary education provision, offering sport and cultural activities alongside the standard curriculum rather than academics alone. Based on Acanthus Circle in Belhar, the school keeps a shorter Friday in its week, open Monday to Thursday from 8am to 3pm and Fridays from 8am to 1pm, closed over weekends.

Bird & Co is a South African fast-food chain known for deboned chicken and wood-fired pizza, a combination that sets it apart from a typical fried-chicken outlet by pairing a full pizza oven with its chicken menu. The chain's own site lists this Kromboom branch among its growing number of locations around Cape Town.

Deboning the chicken before cooking is the signature point of difference for the brand, aimed at customers who want to eat chicken without working around bones, alongside a pizza option for those in a group who want something different. Operating from Kromboom Convenience Centre in Crawford, the outlet trades Sunday to Thursday from 10am to 9pm and Friday and Saturday from 10am to 10pm.

Bloomberg Gym is a fitness and health club offering standard gym facilities alongside group exercise classes, the kind of community-focused gym that competes on accessibility and a loyal local membership rather than a large chain's scale or luxury extras. Clubs of this kind typically combine free weights, cardio equipment and a studio for group sessions such as aerobics or spinning.

Operating from the first floor of Ottery Centre, the gym serves members from Ottery and the surrounding southern suburbs who want a nearby, straightforward fitness option rather than a drive to a bigger national chain gym. It keeps early morning and evening hours on weekdays to suit a working membership, open Monday to Thursday from 6am to 9pm, Fridays from 6am to 8pm, Saturdays from 8am to 4pm and Sundays from 10am to 2pm.

Bobo's Brasserie is a brasserie on the Mouille Point promenade serving French-inspired comfort food such as steak frites, seafood and gourmet burgers, a menu covered in both an Eat Out venue profile and a Crush magazine feature on the restaurant. Its brasserie format sits between a casual eatery and formal fine dining, built around hearty, well-executed classics rather than an experimental tasting menu.

The restaurant's position on the promenade gives diners Atlantic Ocean and Robben Island views alongside their meal, a setting the local food press has singled out as much as the food itself. Based at Two Oceans Beach on Beach Road in Mouille Point, the brasserie trades every day from midday to 10.30pm.

Bok Lounge & Grill is a casual restaurant and grill serving burgers, ribs, pizza and other pub-style fare, available for both dine-in and delivery according to its listing on a local food delivery platform. The grill format covers a broad, crowd-pleasing menu rather than specialising in one cuisine, suited to groups with different tastes ordering together.

The restaurant trades from inside Brackenfell Corner shopping centre, which lists it among its own tenant directory, giving the venue a steady flow of centre shoppers alongside its delivery customer base. Based at Brackenfell Corner on the corner of Frans Conradie Drive and Paradys Street, the restaurant keeps late hours, open Sunday and Monday from 11am to 1am and Tuesday to Saturday from 11am to 2am.
